title: Structured Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Code Generation

title: Activating Latent Security Knowledge through LLM-Guided Risk Analysis for Secure Code Generation
technique_name: BRACE (Black-box Risk Analysis and Contextual Elicitation)
core_idea_checked: Has the model analyze likely security risks of the task (black-box risk analysis) and inserts the elicited CWE-specific guidance into the generation prompt.
gain_metric: Safe Code Rate (fine-tuned classifier), CyberNative, open-weight models
gain_quote: BRACE reaches 91.2%, compared with 33.9% for Secure Prompt.
gain_note: Security judged by a custom fine-tuned classifier; on commercial models 84.3 -> 95.4.
effect_correctness_headline: Its average pass@1 is 79.9%, compared with 79.7% for the unguided baseline
benchmarks: CyberNative Code Vulnerability Security DPO (C++/Java/Python, 142 held-out tasks per language); HumanEval/HumanEval+ (164 tasks); CWEval (119 tasks); BaxBench (392 tasks)
models: Qwen3-8B open instruct; Qwen3-14B open; Qwen3.6-27B open; Gemma-3-4B open; Gemma-3-12B open; Gemma-4-31B open; Claude Haiku 4.5 closed; Claude Sonnet 5 closed; DeepSeek V4 Flash; DeepSeek V4 Pro; GPT-5.6 Luna closed; GPT-5.6 Sol closed
note: Black-box prompting; also reports HumanEval/HumanEval+ correctness.
authors: Xiaoyun Xu; Lichao Wu; Jona te Lintelo; Siyu Zhang; Keke Gai; Stjepan Picek

title: ECO: Enhanced Code Optimization via Performance-Aware Prompting for Code-LLMs
technique_name: ECO (symbolic advisor bottleneck diagnosis + ROI retriever performance-aware prompting)
core_idea_checked: A symbolic advisor diagnoses performance bottlenecks with static analysis and an ROI retriever fetches matching optimization directives, combined into a performance-aware prompt.
gain_quote: on GPT-o4-mini, standard prompting yields only a 1.99× speedup, whereas ECO raises to 7.81×—nearly a four-fold gain.
gain_note: Best of 5; vs instruction-only rather than SBLLM/RAG baselines; fine-tuning beats ECO on 7B.
effect_correctness_headline: Qwen2.5-Coder:7b Best@5 ACC 74.24 vs 68.12 instruction-only; Qwen2.5-Coder:3b ACC 37.80 vs 55.22
benchmarks: PIE C++ test balanced subset (255 tasks); Codeforces C++ OOD (300 tasks from 30 problems); PIE HQ 4,085 pairs as KB
models: Qwen2.5-Coder 3B/7B/14B (open, code-specialized, Q4 quantized); GPT-4o-mini (closed, instruct); GPT-o4-mini (closed, reasoning)
note: C++ (PIE, Codeforces); no own code link found.
authors: Su-Hyeon Kim; Joonghyuk Hahn; Sooyoung Cha; Yo-Sub Han

benchmarks: KernelBench Level 1, 100 problems (also Omni-MATH-2 200 problems, MathVerse 100, non-code)
models: DeepSeek V4 Pro (closed/API, reasoning); DeepSeek V4 Flash (API, reasoning); Qwen3.6-27B (open, reasoning); Claude Opus 5 (closed, reasoning)

title: Fortifying LLM-Based Code Generation with Graph-Based Reasoning on Secure Coding Practices
core_idea_checked: Organizes secure coding practices into a dependency graph and has the LLM traverse relevant practices to revise its seed code.

benchmarks: New benchmark of 54 natural-language prompts (37 Python, 17 C) covering 17 CWEs, 25 samples per scenario; 24 zero-day Python CVE scenarios from the CodeQL Wall of Fame
models: GPT-4o-mini (closed, instruct); Claude-3-haiku (closed, instruct); Gemini-1.5-flash (closed, instruct); Llama-3-8B-Instruct (open, 8B, instruct)
